1. Load in data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Folder containing all CSV files
pilot.data.folder <- "~/GitHub/sporeAI/data/infection.pilot_predictions_newlabels/csv"

# Get all CSV files
files <- list.files(
  path = pilot.data.folder,
  pattern = "\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
# Since folder contains .csvs
all_data <- map_dfr(files, function(file) {

  filename <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))

  dat <- read_csv(file, show_col_types = FALSE)

  parts <- str_split(filename, "_")[[1]]

  dat %>%
    mutate(
      Treatment = parts[1],
      Time = as.numeric(str_remove(parts[2], "T")),
      Stage = if_else(
        "preinfect" %in% parts,
        "preinfect",
        "postinfect"
      ),
      Replicate = as.numeric(parts[length(parts)]),
      File = filename
    )
})
```

```{r}

  count(Treatment, Flask, Time, Image, name) %>%

    percent = n / total * 100
```

## Initial thoughts
- This pilot experiment likely does not capture the full sporulation window: Across all experimental flasks, mature spores are very low, I expected to see an increase in mature spores over time across all treatments (especially the control), this indicates to me that I did not capture the full sporulation window (which was my initial gut feeling when looking a the images--I want to continue experiment to image hours 8-16)
- On this same note, even though late stage spores and mature spore abundance is low, it’s the highest (accounts for ~ 35% ) in early infection treatment at t = 5 which is curious
- Early infection shows a pronounced decline in vegetative cells between approx T2-T5, this could be a signal of lysis maybe, and that is interestingly accompanied by an increase in stage 4 spores
- I wasn’t expecting late-infection treatment to show a rather consistent amount of vegetative cells over time, I think this could be due to the model not yet trained on stage 1 of sporulation (since veg. cells and stage 1 cells are phenotyptically similar), however if this persists it could be indicative of some sort of stalling of the progression of sporulation

########################################################################

PART 2: ABSORBING STATE FRAMEWORK/STAGE STRUCTURE MODELING
filt.data contains the name of the predicted sporulation stage, the sampling time, treatment, model confidence for classification, experimental replicates etc which should be enough info to quantify stage structure over time 

A. Calculate the observed stage distributions 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

stage_counts <- filt.data %>%
  mutate(
    name = factor(name, levels = stage_levels)
  ) %>%
  count(
    Treatment, BioRep, Flask, Time, name,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  complete(
    nesting(Treatment, BioRep, Flask, Time),
    name = factor(stage_levels, levels = stage_levels),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, BioRep, Flask, Time) %>%
  mutate(
    total_cells = sum(n),
    proportion = n / total_cells
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```
B. Fit a stage structured model (this might be difficult given that we do not have a failure state, so we have to start with a model that has successful completion as the only absorbing state)
```{r}
stage_summary <- stage_counts %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Time, name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_proportion = mean(proportion, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stage_plot <- ggplot(
  stage_summary,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = mean_proportion,
    fill = name
  )
) +
  geom_area(
    position = "stack",
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Proportion of classified cells",
    fill = "Sporulation stage"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

stage_plot
```
```{r}
stage_counts %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Time, name) %>%
  summarise(
    total_n = sum(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = name,
    values_from = total_n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```
Minor issue: in the current data we are working with (which is pilot data) the stages are not monotonically progressing, meaning that in the early infection treatment, spore fraction rises, and declines, and then increases later again, i.e., the amount of complete cells entering the absorbing state should not decrease over time and our observations violate that prediction so becasue of this, we will work with a 3-state absorbing model, vegetative cells, sporulating (middle stages) and complete spore
```{r}
# Create simplified states
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

stage3_data <- filt.data %>%
  mutate(
    State = case_when(
      name == "vegetative" ~ "Vegetative",
      name %in% paste0("stage", 1:5) ~ "Sporulating",
      name == "complete" ~ "Complete",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(State))
# Calculate proportions
stage3_counts <- stage3_data %>%
  count(
    Treatment, BioRep, Flask, Time, State,
    name = "n"
  ) %>%
  complete(
    nesting(Treatment, BioRep, Flask, Time),
    State = c("Vegetative", "Sporulating", "Complete"),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, BioRep, Flask, Time) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    proportion = n / total
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Summarize across samples
stage3_summary <- stage3_counts %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Time, State) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_prop = mean(proportion),
    sd_prop = sd(proportion),
    n_samples = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Plot trajectories
ggplot(
  stage3_summary,
  aes(
    x = Time,
    y = mean_prop,
    color = State
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Proportion of classified cells",
    color = "Cell state"
  )
```

```{r}
completion_check %>%

```
Fit model to observations
```{r}
library(deSolve)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```
Prepare observed stage proportions
```{r}
stages <- c(
  "vegetative", "stage1", "stage2",
  "stage3", "stage4", "stage5", "complete"
)

observed <- filt.data %>%
  filter(name %in% stages) %>%
  count(Treatment, Time, name, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    nesting(Treatment, Time),
    name = stages,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Time) %>%
  mutate(proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()
```
Define stage-structured model of sporulation using ODE (underlying assumption: cells progress sequentially through sporulation, with completed spores representing an absorbed state, assuming constant transition rates (to simplify), no cell death or lysis, no developmental arrest as a separate fate )
```{r}
sporulation_model <- function(t, state, parameters) { # defining the function called sporulation_model which accepts 3 inputs: simulation time, state, and parameters which are the transition rates between stages 

  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {

    dvegetative <- -k0 * vegetative # describes the rate of change in the vegetative population (negative sign indicates that cells are leaving this state as sporulation is initiated) NOTE: this model assumes that veg cells decrease because they are entering sporulation and no other reason

    dstage1 <- k0 * vegetative - k1 * stage1 # the rate at which veg cells enter stage 1
    dstage2 <- k1 * stage1 - k2 * stage2 # the rate at which stage 1 cells progress to stage 2
    dstage3 <- k2 * stage2 - k3 * stage3 # the rate at which stage 2 cells progress to stage 3
    dstage4 <- k3 * stage3 - k4 * stage4 # the rate at which stage 3 cells progress to stage 4
    dstage5 <- k4 * stage4 - k5 * stage5 # the rate at which stage 4 cells progress to stage 5 

    dcomplete <- k5 * stage5 # the accumulation of completed spores (no negative term because spores cannot leave this state)

    list(c( # return the 7 calculated rates of change to the ODE solver, the solver uses these derivatives to estimate how the pop. changes over time
      dvegetative,
      dstage1,
      dstage2,
      dstage3,
      dstage4,
      dstage5,
      dcomplete
    ))
  })
}
```

```{r}
fit_sporulation <- function(treatment_name) { # defining the fitting function based on treatment group (control, early infection, or late) it fits each treatment independently

  obs <- observed %>% # take the previously observed dataframe and perform two operations 1) select the observations for each treatment and 2) sort observations by time and then by developmental stage 
    filter(Treatment == treatment_name) %>%
    arrange(Time, match(name, stages)) # return the position of each stage within that vector this is important becasue the model contains multiple state variables and the order must match the order used when extracting observations to generate predictions

  times <- sort(unique(obs$Time)) # identify observation times for which ODE will calculate predictions (time represents hours after DSM resuspension)

  initial <- obs %>% # Define initial conditions the ODE needs to know the state of the system at the beginning of the simulation 
    filter(Time == min(Time)) %>% # select the first time point (selects obs from the earliest sampling time)
    arrange(match(name, stages)) %>% # arrange stages in developmental order
    pull(proportion) # extract proportions 

  names(initial) <- stages # assign corresponding stage names (initialize the model using the actual observed stage proportions at t=0)

  objective <- function(log_rates) { # define the objective function which is the central part of the model fitting procedure (i.e., how well a particular set of model params reproduces the observations with the goal being to find the transition rates that minimize the discrepency between predicted and observed state proportions)

    rates <- exp(log_rates) # the objective function takes an argument called log_rates, we do this because because we have 6 transition rates and these rates should not be negative (negative would imply that cells can move backward in the process)
    names(rates) <- paste0("k", 0:5) 

    prediction <- tryCatch( # simulate sporulation using the proposed rates (where the fitting function called the ODE model)
      ode( # numerically solves the diff. equations in the sporulation model with the following arguments, the ODE solver then calculates how to pop would progress through sporulation under those rates, it produces predicted proportions for each stage at every sampling time 
        y = initial,
        times = times,
        func = sporulation_model,
        parms = rates
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL # if error occurs return NULL instead of stopping entire optimization
    )

    if (is.null(prediction)) return(1e12)

    prediction <- as.data.frame(prediction) #organize model predictions

    predicted <- as.matrix( # select the 7 develop,mental stage columns
      prediction[, stages]
    )

    actual <- obs %>% # organize the observed data in the same format (same structure as predicted )
      select(Time, name, proportion) %>%
      pivot_wider(
        names_from = name,
        values_from = proportion
      ) %>%
      arrange(Time) %>%
      select(all_of(stages)) %>% # ensures columns are in correct developmental order
      as.matrix() # converts data frame into numeric matrix

    sum((predicted - actual)^2) # calculate the difference between predictions and obs
  }

  fit <- optim( # find transition rates that minimize error 
    par = log(rep(0.2, 6)),
    fn = objective,
    method = "BFGS"
  )

  rates <- exp(fit$par) # extract fitted transitions, resulting values represent the estimated transition rates, model-inferred and not directly observed
  names(rates) <- paste0("k", 0:5)

  list( # return list containing all components 
    treatment = treatment_name,
    rates = rates,
    initial = initial,
    fit = fit
  )
}
# fit_sporulation function performs parm estimation by min. sum of squared differences between observed and ODE predicted sporulation stage proportions 
# sporulation_model defines how cells are assumed to progress through sporulation 
# fit_sporulation estimates which transition rates best reproduce the observed populaton comp. under those assumptions 
```

```{r}
# Run the fit sporulation function separately for each treatment, store results, and extract estimated transition rates 
fits <- lapply( # fit the model to each treatment, apply to every element in the vector list 
  unique(observed$Treatment), # extract unique treatment names from df
  fit_sporulation # each call fits the 7 state sporulation model to the treatment's observed stage proportions 
)

names(fits) <- unique(observed$Treatment) # name fitted models

lapply(fits, function(x) x$rates) # extract the transition rates, the numbers outputted are 
```
Use fitted rates to simulate predicted stage distributions
```{r}
simulate_sporulation <- function(fit_object) { # define the simulation function and use fit object which are the results from the model fitting

  times <- seq(0, 48, by = 0.25) # define simulation times 

  prediction <- ode( # simulate sporulation using the fitted parms
    y = fit_object$initial,
    times = times,
    func = sporulation_model,
    parms = fit_object$rates # estimated transition rates from the fitting procedure
  )

  as.data.frame(prediction) %>% # ODE will return a matrix like object --> convert to df
    pivot_longer( # convert from wide to long
      cols = all_of(stages),
      names_to = "name",
      values_to = "predicted"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Treatment = fit_object$treatment)
}

simulated <- bind_rows( # simulate all 3 treatments 
  lapply(fits, simulate_sporulation)
)
```

Determining if absorbing state model describes sporulation data based on goodness of fit, residual analysis
```{r}
predicted_at_obs <- bind_rows( # generate predictions at the observed sampling times 
  lapply(fits, function(f) {

    times <- sort(unique( # extracts the sampling times for each treatment 
      observed$Time[
        observed$Treatment == f$treatment
      ]
    ))

    pred <- ode( # generate model predicitons 
      y = f$initial,
      times = times,
      func = sporulation_model,
      parms = f$rates
    )

    as.data.frame(pred) %>% # reshape the predictions 
      pivot_longer(
        cols = all_of(stages),
        names_to = "name",
        values_to = "predicted"
      ) %>%
      mutate(Treatment = f$treatment)
  })
)

comparison <- observed %>% # combine predictions with observations 
  left_join(
    predicted_at_obs,
    by = c(
      "Treatment",
      "Time" = "time",
      "name"
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate( # calculate redisuals 
    residual = proportion - predicted
  )

# Calculate RMSE and mean absolute error
fit_metrics <- comparison %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(residual^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(residual)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fit_metrics
# Let's check to see what stages the model struggles to reproduce 
stage_fit_metrics <- comparison %>%
  group_by(Treatment, name) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(residual^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(residual)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stage_fit_metrics
```

RMSE: Root mean squared error -- sensitivity to large errors is higher
MAE: Mean absolute error -- sensistivity to large errors is lower
Lower RMSE and MAEW values indicate that the fitted model more closely reproduces the observed proportions 

For the control: relatively small overall differences between observed and predicted stage proportions

For early infecton: this is much larger and suggests that the model has more difficulty reproducing the stage ditriubutions under early infection 

Late infection: intermediate level of prediction error

Posterior predictive style model check (used to investigate whether the decreases in completed spore proportions could arise from sampling variability under the fitted model)
```{r}
largest_drop <- function(p) { # this function measures the largest decrease between consec. obs. 
  max(c(0, -diff(p)))
}

```

```{r}

  group_by(Treatment, Time) %>%
  mutate(

  ) %>%

comparison %>%

```

```{r}
set.seed(123) #ensures that the random numbers generated during the sim are reproducible 

check_completion <- function(treatment_name, nsim = 1000) { # define model checking function

  dat <- comparison %>%
    filter(
      Treatment == treatment_name,
      name == "complete"
    ) %>%
    arrange(Time)

  observed_drop <- largest_drop(dat$proportion)

  simulated_drops <- replicate(nsim, {

    simulated_complete <- rbinom(
      n = nrow(dat),
      size = dat$total_cells,
      prob = pmin(pmax(dat$predicted, 0), 1)
    ) / dat$total_cells

    largest_drop(simulated_complete)
  })

  data.frame(
    Treatment = treatment_name,
    Observed_drop = observed_drop,
    Simulated_95th_percentile =
      unname(quantile(simulated_drops, 0.95)),
    Tail_probability =
      mean(simulated_drops >= observed_drop)
  )
}

completion_checks <- bind_rows(
  lapply(unique(comparison$Treatment), check_completion)
)

completion_checks
```
Tail prob: fraction of simulated datasets in which the largest decrease was at least as large as the observed decrease
i.e., none of the simulated datasets produced a drop this large 

Okay these results above tell us that the current absobring state model does not adequately reproduce the dynamics we see, likely because the model is too restrictive to our observations, we likely need to include cell turnover, we are currently working with a model that does not allow for cells to enter the population even though division is likely occurring in our samples so instead of assuming a closed population, we need to assume a model with turnover

###### APPROACH 2: 3 STAGE MODEL #########
What is changing here: we are simplifying the stages to see if that more accurately represents the pop dynamics 
We also introduce a veg. growth parmater, r, allowing veg population to increase which is important because now this is no longer a closed population Note that this model still does not account for cell lysis or cell death 

Observed 3 state data (reorganize data to fit with simplified model)
Here we are converting the cell level microscopy classification to 3 state dataset containing counts and proportions for each treatment and sampling time 
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(deSolve)

states3 <- c("Vegetative", "Sporulating", "Complete") # define 3 developmental states

observed3 <- filt.data %>% # reclassify cells into three states 
  mutate(
    State = case_when(
      name == "vegetative" ~ "Vegetative",
      name %in% paste0("stage", 1:5) ~ "Sporulating", # if a cell is classified as stage 1, 2, 3, 4 etc. reclassify as sporulating
      name == "complete" ~ "Complete",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(State)) %>% # remove cells without recognized classification
  count(Treatment, Time, State, name = "n") %>% # count the number of cells in each state 
  complete( # ensure all three states appear at every sampling time 
    nesting(Treatment, Time),
    State = states3,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Time) %>% # calculate total cells and proportions 
  mutate(
    total_cells = sum(n),
    proportion = n / total_cells
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Check
```{r}
observed3 %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Early infection") %>%
  print(n = 15)
```
Define population model
(some model limitations to keep in mind: growth is exponential, transition rates are constant, progression is irreversible, completed spores remain absorbing, there is no lysis or cell death)
```{r}
population_model <- function(t, state, parameters) { # function called pop model 

  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {

    dVegetative <- r * Vegetative - k1 * Vegetative # model veg cells here r is the per capita veg growth rate (no nutrient limitation or carrying capacity)

    dSporulating <- k1 * Vegetative - k2 * Sporulating # model sporulating cells

    dComplete <- k2 * Sporulating # model cells completing sporulation

    list(c( # return derivatives to the ODE solver
      dVegetative,
      dSporulating,
      dComplete
    ))
  })
}
```
Fit model to each treatment (estimate parms)
```{r}
fit_population <- function(treatment_name) { # create function to fit model 

  obs <- observed3 %>%
    filter(Treatment == treatment_name) # select observations for each treatment

  counts <- obs %>% # restructure obs to a count matrix
    select(Time, State, n) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = State,
      values_from = n,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    arrange(Time)

  times <- counts$Time # extract sampling times

  y0 <- as.numeric( # define the initial conditions 
    counts[1, states3]
  )

  y0 <- y0 / sum(y0) # normalize the initial conditions 
  names(y0) <- states3 # name the elements 

  objective <- function(log_parameters) { # define the objective function 

    parameters <- exp(log_parameters) # convert parms to log scale 
    names(parameters) <- c("r", "k1", "k2")

    prediction <- tryCatch( # solve the model using proposed parameters 
      ode(
        y = y0,
        times = times,
        func = population_model,
        parms = parameters
      ),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )

    if (is.null(prediction)) return(1e12)

    pred <- as.matrix( # extract predicted pop size 
      as.data.frame(prediction)[, states3]
    )

    pred <- pred / rowSums(pred) # convert model predictions into proportions 
    pred <- pmax(pred, 1e-12)
    pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)

    observed_counts <- as.matrix( # extract the observed cell counts
      counts[, states3]
    )

    -sum(observed_counts * log(pred)) # calculate negative log liklihood 
  }

  fit <- optim( # optimize parms
    par = log(c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)),
    fn = objective,
    method = "Nelder-Mead",
    control = list(maxit = 10000)
  )

  parameters <- exp(fit$par) # extract fitted parms
  names(parameters) <- c("r", "k1", "k2")

  list( # return the fitted model 
    treatment = treatment_name,
    parameters = parameters,
    initial = y0,
    fit = fit
  )
}
```

Fit the 3 state model to each of the experimental treatments
```{r}
fits3 <- lapply( # fit the model to each treatment 
  unique(observed3$Treatment),
  fit_population
)

names(fits3) <- unique(observed3$Treatment) # name the fitted models

lapply(fits3, function(x) x$parameters) #extract the fitted parms

# Verify that the optimization converged 
lapply(fits3, function(x) x$fit$convergence)
```
Simulate fitted model over 48 h to estimate the proportions of veg. cells sporulating cells, and completed cells 
```{r}
simulate_population <- function(fit_object) { # define simulation function

  prediction <- ode( # solve differential equations 
    y = fit_object$initial,
    times = seq(0, 48, by = 0.25),
    func = population_model,
    parms = fit_object$parameters
  )

  prediction <- as.data.frame(prediction) # convert simulation output to dataframe

  prediction <- prediction %>% # calculate the total modeled pop
    mutate(
      total = Vegetative + Sporulating + Complete
    ) %>%
    mutate( # convert predicted pops into proportions
      across(
        all_of(states3),
        ~ .x / total
      )
    )

  prediction %>% # convert preditions into long format
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(states3),
      names_to = "State",
      values_to = "predicted"
    ) %>%
    mutate(Treatment = fit_object$treatment) # identify the simulated treatments 
}

simulated3 <- bind_rows( # simulate all 3 fitted models
  lapply(fits3, simulate_population)
)
```

What can we learn from the above output? (Interpret with caution, given that that model does not fit that well)
r: vegetative growth rate 
In the control treatment, the model estimated essentially no vegetative growth, but estimated positive veg. growth for both infection treatments 
BUT  it is difficult to draw this conclusion becasue we didn't measure absolute pop. growth. instead we estimated growth from changes in the relative proportions of developmental states 

k1: the rate at which veg. cells enter sporulation, both infection treatments have higher estimated initiation rates than the control (while this is enticing to say that infected cells enter sporulatiuon earflier I am not sure if that is okay to draw on here )
I.e., the late infection rate is 2.6 times the control estimate 

k2 is our sporulation rate; within the model, cells in the late infection treatment transition from teh combined sporulating state to the completed sporulating state more rapidly, but becasue we combined the intermediate stages, this is the effective transition rate across the entire sporulating category  

In order to draw any light conclusuons from this, we should make sure that the model can reliably estimate individual parms

```{r}
control_fit <- fits3[["Control"]]

control_fit$parameters

# Create a rangle of candidate values for r 
r_values <- seq(
  from = 0, 
  to = 0.2, 
  by = 0.005
)

r_values

# Prep observed cell counts
control_counts <- observed3 %>%
  filter(Treatment == "Control") %>%
  select(Time, State, n) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = State,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(Time)

control_counts

# Create function that calcs the negative log-liklihood while holding r fixed

# define the initial conditions and samp times
control_times <- control_counts$Time

control_y0 <- as.numeric(control_counts[1, states3])
control_y0 <- control_y0 / sum(control_y0)
names(control_y0) <- states3

# define the neg. log-liklihood 
profile_nll <- function(log_k, fixed_r) {

  parameters <- c(
    r = fixed_r,
    k1 = exp(log_k[1]),
    k2 = exp(log_k[2])
  )

  prediction <- tryCatch(
    ode(
      y = control_y0,
      times = control_times,
      func = population_model,
      parms = parameters
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  if (is.null(prediction)) return(1e12)

  pred <- as.matrix(
    as.data.frame(prediction)[, states3]
  )

  pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)
  pred <- pmax(pred, 1e-12)
  pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)

  observed_counts <- as.matrix(control_counts[, states3])

  -sum(observed_counts * log(pred))
}

# Construct parameters
profile_nll <- function(log_k, fixed_r) {

  parameters <- c(
    r = fixed_r,
    k1 = exp(log_k[1]),
    k2 = exp(log_k[2])
  )

  # Solve ODE
  prediction <- tryCatch(
    ode(
      y = control_y0,
      times = control_times,
      func = population_model,
      parms = parameters
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )

  # Return a large penalty if the ODE solver fails
  if (is.null(prediction)) return(1e12)

  # Extract predicted state abundances
  pred <- as.matrix(
    as.data.frame(prediction)[, states3]
  )

  # Convert predictions to proportions
  pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)

  # Prevent numerical issues with log(0)
  pred <- pmax(pred, 1e-12)
  pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)

  # Extract observed cell counts
  observed_counts <- as.matrix(control_counts[, states3])

  # Calculate negative log-likelihood
  -sum(observed_counts * log(pred))

}

profile_nll(
  log_k = log(c(0.014, 0.157)),
  fixed_r = 0.05
)

test_fit <- optim(
  par = log(c(0.014, 0.157)),
  fn = profile_nll,
  fixed_r = 0.05,
  method = "Nelder-Mead"
)

test_fit

```

```{r}
    k1 = exp(fit$par[1]),
    k2 = exp(fit$par[2]),

  )

})
```

###### APPROACH 3 #########

Modify to allow cells to enter sporulation at different rates during early and late phases 
```{r}
population_model_time <- function(t, state, parameters) {

  with(as.list(c(state, parameters)), {

   k1 <- if (t < t_switch) k_early else k_late

    dVegetative <- r * Vegetative - k1 * Vegetative

    dSporulating <- k1 * Vegetative - k2 * Sporulating

    dComplete <- k2 * Sporulating

    list(c(
      dVegetative,
      dSporulating,
      dComplete
    ))
  })
}
```

```{r}
fit_population_time <- function(treatment_name, t_switch) { # allow for different sporilation initiation switching times

  obs <- observed3 %>%
    filter(Treatment == treatment_name)

  counts <- obs %>%
    select(Time, State, n) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = State,
      values_from = n,
      values_fill = 0
    ) %>%
    arrange(Time)

  times <- counts$Time

  y0 <- as.numeric(counts[1, states3])
  y0 <- y0 / sum(y0)
  names(y0) <- states3

  objective <- function(log_parameters) {

parameters <- exp(log_parameters) # estimate rate parms
names(parameters) <- c(
  "r", "k_early", "k_late", "k2"
)

parameters <- c(parameters, t_switch = t_switch)

prediction <- tryCatch(
  ode(
    y = y0,
    times = sort(unique(c(times, t_switch))),
    func = population_model_time,
    parms = parameters
  ),
  error = function(e) NULL
)
    if (is.null(prediction)) return(1e12)

    prediction <- as.data.frame(prediction) %>%
      filter(time %in% times)

    pred <- as.matrix(prediction[, states3])

    pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)
    pred <- pmax(pred, 1e-12)
    pred <- pred / rowSums(pred)

    observed_counts <- as.matrix(counts[, states3])

    -sum(observed_counts * log(pred)) 
  }

  fit <- optim(
    par = log(c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1)),
    fn = objective,
    method = "Nelder-Mead",
    control = list(maxit = 10000)
  )

  parameters <- exp(fit$par)
  names(parameters) <- c(
    "r", "k_early", "k_late", "k2"
  )

list(
  treatment = treatment_name,
  t_switch = t_switch,
  parameters = parameters,
  initial = y0,
  fit = fit
)
}
```

```{r}
          t_switch = x$t_switch,
          r = x$parameters["r"],
          k_early = x$parameters["k_early"],
          k_late = x$parameters["k_late"],
          k2 = x$parameters["k2"],
          NLL = x$fit$value,
          convergence = x$fit$convergence
        )

      })
    )
  })
)

parameter_table_time

# Identify best fitting model 
best_switch_times <- parameter_table_time %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  slice_min(NLL, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

best_switch_times

```

```{r}
# Extract the best-fitting model for each treatment
best_fits_time <- lapply(fits_time, function(treatment_fits) {
  treatment_fits[[which.min(
    sapply(treatment_fits, function(x) x$fit$value)
  )]]
})

# Generate predictions from the best-fitting models
predictions_time <- bind_rows(
  lapply(best_fits_time, function(x) {

    times <- sort(unique(c(
      observed3$Time[observed3$Treatment == x$treatment],
      x$t_switch
    )))

    parameters <- c(
      x$parameters,
      t_switch = x$t_switch
    )

    ode(
      y = x$initial,
      times = times,
      func = population_model_time,
      parms = parameters
    ) %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      mutate(
        Treatment = x$treatment
      )
  })
)
```

Convert preditions to proportions
```{r}
predictions_time_long <- predictions_time %>%
  mutate(
    total = Vegetative + Sporulating + Complete
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(states3),
    names_to = "State",
    values_to = "abundance"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    proportion = abundance / total
  )
```


```{r}
approach3_plot <- ggplot() +

  # Model predictions
  geom_line(
    data = predictions_time_long,
    aes(
      x = time,

      color = State
    ),

  ) +

  # Observed microscopy proportions
  geom_point(
    data = observed3,

    ),
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "",
    subtitle = "",
    x = "Time (h)",
    y = "Proportion of cells",
    color = "Cell state"
  )

approach3_plot
```



```{r}
# Compare goodness of fit against constant rate model 
predicted_time_at_obs <- predictions_time_long %>%
  filter(time %in% unique(observed3$Time)) %>%
  rename(
    Time = time,
    predicted = proportion
  ) %>%
  select(Treatment, Time, State, predicted)

comparison_time <- observed3 %>%
  left_join(
    predicted_time_at_obs,
    by = c("Treatment", "Time", "State")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    residual = proportion - predicted
  )

fit_metrics_time <- comparison_time %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(residual^2)),
    MAE = mean(abs(residual)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

fit_metrics_time
```
Compare 
```{r}
fit_metrics3 %>%
  rename(
    RMSE_constant = RMSE,
    MAE_constant = MAE
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    fit_metrics_time %>%
      rename(
        RMSE_time = RMSE,
        MAE_time = MAE
      ),
    by = "Treatment"
  )
```

Comparing model 2 approach (fits3 to this approach)

```{r}
# Extract negative log-likelihoods from Approach 2
nll_approach2 <- data.frame(
  Treatment = sapply(fits3, function(x) x$treatment),
  NLL = sapply(fits3, function(x) x$fit$value)
)

nll_approach2
```

AIC

```{r}
# Approach 2: 3 parameters
aic_approach2 <- nll_approach2 %>%
  mutate(
    Model = "Approach 2",
    AIC = 2 * 3 + 2 * NLL
  )

# Approach 3: 5 parameters
aic_approach3 <- best_switch_times %>%
  mutate(
    Model = "Approach 3",
    AIC = 2 * 5 + 2 * NLL
  )

# Combine results
aic_comparison <- bind_rows(
  aic_approach2 %>%
    select(Treatment, Model, AIC),
  aic_approach3 %>%
    select(Treatment, Model, AIC)
)

aic_comparison
```

PART 3: FITTING TO GAM (because GAM does not assume that cells progress through stages at constant rates)
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(mgcv)
```

Define stage order and prep counts
```{r}
stages <- c(
  "vegetative",
  "stage1",
  "stage2",
  "stage3",
  "stage4",
  "stage5",
  "complete"
)

gam_data <- filt.data %>%
  filter(name %in% stages) %>%
  mutate(
    name = factor(name, levels = stages),
    Treatment = factor(Treatment)
  ) %>%
  count(Treatment, Time, name, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    nesting(Treatment, Time),
    name = factor(stages, levels = stages),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, Time) %>%
  mutate(
    total = sum(n),
    proportion = n / total
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Fit GAM separately for each treatment
```{r}
gam_cells <- filt.data %>%
  filter(name %in% stages) %>%
  mutate(
    Stage = match(name, stages) - 1L,
    Treatment = factor(Treatment)
  )

fit_stage_gam <- function(treatment_name) {

  dat <- gam_cells %>%
    filter(Treatment == treatment_name)

  gam(
    list(
      Stage ~ s(Time, k = 6, bs = "cr"),
      ~ s(Time, k = 6, bs = "cr"),
      ~ s(Time, k = 6, bs = "cr"),
      ~ s(Time, k = 6, bs = "cr"),
      ~ s(Time, k = 6, bs = "cr"),
      ~ s(Time, k = 6, bs = "cr")
    ),
    family = multinom(K = 6),
    data = dat,
    method = "REML"
  )
}

gam_fits <- lapply(
  levels(gam_cells$Treatment),
  fit_stage_gam
)

names(gam_fits) <- levels(gam_cells$Treatment)
```
